source_notes: This rubric is built from two kinds of real, openly-published source: (1) University of London's own live programme materials for the LLM Postgraduate Laws route (module short-course pages and the 2026-27 Programme Regulations), and (2) the UK sector-wide QAA Master's Degree Characteristics Statement (February 2020). UoL's detailed module study guides, module-specific examiners' reports, and the numeric marking-band descriptors in the gated 'Appendix D - Assessment criteria' were not accessible; this course does not invent numbers or descriptors to fill that gap.

Assessment facts carried over: each of the four sub-modules (A-D) within a module is separately assessed by a 45-minute (plus 10 minutes' reading time) unseen closed-book written examination, with no coursework component; pass mark 50% per module (40-49% occasionally condoned at the Board of Examiners' discretion); merit requires an average of 60-69% with at least half of contributing modules at 60%+; distinction requires an average of 70%+ with at least half at 70%+; maximum two attempts per module, examinations sit twice yearly (May and October), the higher mark is taken.

LWM36 (International Trade Law) is, as UoL actually defines it, a private-law module about the network of contracts (sale, carriage, finance) needed to move goods across borders, not a public international trade law/WTO module (GATT, trade remedies, dispute panels) -- that subject matter belongs to a different UoL module. This course stays faithful to LWM36's real, confirmed scope.

Case law and statutes cited throughout are real, well-known primary authority (CJEU/General Court, English courts, EU regulations/directives and UK statutes), verified from their own primary text via EUR-Lex, legislation.gov.uk and BAILII rather than from UoL's gated numbering.
